notes: Concerns, none failing a stated requirement. (1) The telemetry worker thread is non-daemon, so at process exit the interpreter waits for the whole backlog (up to 256 jobs) to drain; with 20 presses and a 0.5 s exporter exit took about 12.7 s, and an exporter that never returns would block exit forever. Real OTLP exporters have timeouts, but T8.7 should call flush(timeout) and consider a bounded shutdown. (2) Queued jobs hold the Card (suggestion, evidence quotes, so transcript-derived text) until the worker runs them: at most 256 cards, normally milliseconds, longer if the exporter is stalled. A conversation delete does not purge them; the text stays in process memory only and is never exported, so low privacy risk. (3) A dropped press logs a warning but increments no counter, so a drop is visible only in logs. (4) Stage deltas are computed as ctx.stage_ms minus a snapshot; Team and Single assign (not accumulate) their stage keys, so a Context reused across presses with identical values gives a zero or negative delta (a reused ctx gave duration -1 and moved tokens to 'other'). The only caller today (replay/runner.py:49) builds a fresh Context per press; T8.7's backend must do the same. (5) The scene note SceneStore.delete is not yet wired into T8.2's delete; the docstring says T8.7 wires it. The card is read on the worker thread while a caller could in theory mutate it after return (nothing does). No secrets and no legacy/ changes in the diff. The single-agent 'suggestion' stage span was not exercised by my stubs (the card was answered without a suggestion call) but the existing stage-span tests and the stage key logic cover it.
